provenance.real_time: none: no real-time train positions, delays or crowding were available or used

licence.name: Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0

selection.way_rule: OSM ways of Overture rail segments, ways of route relations (route in ['light_rail', 'railway', 'subway', 'train', 'tram']) touching them, platform/station ways of those routes, of stop areas and of Overture transit infrastructure
selection.relation_rule: route relations with a way among the Overture rail ways; their route_master; public_transport=stop_area with a member among the Overture/route ids or among the scanned features
selection.node_rule: all nodes of kept ways (any location) plus nodes inside the bbox with station/entrance/platform/stop railway or public_transport tags (full scan of the node stripes)

timetables.source: DfT Bus Open Data Service (BODS) UK aggregate GTFS, Mobility Database mirror
timetables.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (Bus Open Data Service, Department for Transport)
timetables.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (Bus Open Data Service, Department for Transport)
timetables.service_date_selection: Same representative Thursday as the BODS bus subset (gtfs_bods/index.json); all eleven Underground lines run on it.

feed_coverage.rule: rail-like route_type (0-2, 100-199, 400-499, 900-999) whose route short name maps to the line, or whose agency name contains 'Overground'

timetables.time_resolution: GTFS times are whole minutes with arrival == departure (no dwell times in the feed)
timetables.nature: Scheduled timetable (working timetable as published in BODS GTFS); not real-time, no train positions, no crowding

depth_model.nature: assumed: no measured track or platform depths were available; every tunnel depth below is a typical value, flagged depth_source 'assumed_typical'
depth_model.tunnel: OSM tunnel=yes (also covered/culvert) marks underground sections; covered=yes and building_passage count as surface
depth_model.line_kind: sub-surface (cut-and-cover): District, Circle, Hammersmith & City, Metropolitan; deep-level tube: Bakerloo, Central, Jubilee, Northern, Piccadilly, Victoria, Waterloo & City; Elizabeth/Overground/national rail: rail
depth_model.layers: OSM layer is relative: each line's length-weighted most common tunnel layer is its reference at the typical depth; each layer below/above adds/removes 6.0 m, clamped to 1 step shallower and 2 steps deeper, within [3.0, 40.0] m
depth_model.unknown_line: tunnels without a line from OSM route relations use the sub-surface depth (railway=subway) or the rail tunnel depth (depth_source 'assumed_typical_line_unknown')
depth_model.portals: depth rises linearly from 0 at a portal (vertex shared with a non-tunnel way) to the tunnel depth over 200.0 m into the tunnel; layer changes between tunnels ramp with the same gradient
depth_model.bridges: bridge/viaduct or layer > 0: +6.0 m per layer (as the road model's 6.5 m deck), ramped down over 100.0 m onto the approaches
depth_model.surface: all other track at z = 0 (embankments and cuttings not modelled; flat ground, no terrain)
depth_model.stations: platform level = assumed track level at the platform

colours.source: TfL line colour standard (reference constants in transit.underground.config.LINES); Waterloo & City #93CEBA, Overground #EE7C0E

provenance.coordinates: scene ENU metres (tfl.Enu equirectangular about the scene origin); z metres on the scene DEM: surface track and entrances on the street surface (river filled from the banks), tunnels at the assumed depth below a 150 m low-pass of that surface, blended over the first 6 m at portals; stations carry surface_z (street level above them)
provenance.domain: |x|, |y| <= 4000 m; tracks/platforms clipped at the boundary; the track graph extends 1500 m beyond it for continuity
